name: jobs_pilot
_notes: cells = 6-digit SOC occupations (one occupation per market; 2-digit groups gave ~2 feasible postings per seeker). Local (in-office/partial) 2025 postings: 291141 registered nurses 173k; 533032 heavy-truck drivers 72k; 412031 retail salespersons 54k; 311131 nursing assistants 35k. Chosen for wage spread. High-wage sensitivity: 113031 financial managers 58k, 151252 software developers 29k.
months: two development months only. Never point a config at 2025-08..2025-12 before the design is frozen.
Exposure names are keyed into saved recommendations; do not rename llm_k5 after a submit.
reverse_delete precedes exact_* so the incumbent warm start is set.
llm_k5 is skipped (not failed) until results/llm/jobs_pilot/recs.jsonl exists.
level_gap=2 is feasibility condition (iv); the nolevel variant (99) is the pay-floor-only rule for comparison.

posting_band=top oversamples the top salary quartile, since the pay floor binds higher-wage seekers. bottomband reproduces the housing-style oversample (run 2 of the pilot); natural uses no stratification.
